10	# The étale-sheafified relative Picard functor
11	
12	This file constructs the **étale-sheafified relative Picard functor**
13	`Pic_{(C/k)ét}` of a smooth proper curve `C/k` and proves that it *is* a sheaf
14	for the étale topology — the object whose representability is the project's
15	central open obligation (`Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean`).
16	
17	## Why the sheafification is the right object
18	
19	The relative Picard presheaf `T ↦ Pic(C ×_k T)/π_T^* Pic(T)`
20	(`Scheme.PicSharp.relPresheaf`, Kleiman §2 Def. `df:Pfs`) is in general **not
21	a sheaf**, not even for the Zariski topology (Kleiman §2, L1292–L1302): a line
22	bundle on `C ×_k T` can be trivial on each member of a cover of `T` without
23	being trivial modulo `π_T^* Pic(T)`, because the gluing data is a `Pic`-class
24	of the overlaps. Kleiman's representability theorem (§4 Thm. `th:main`) is
25	therefore a statement about the associated **étale** sheaf, and it is that
26	statement which is true over an arbitrary base field with no rational-point
27	hypothesis.
28	
29	There are two ways to reach a sheaf, and they differ in what has to be
30	supplied:
31	
32	1. assume `C` has a `k`-rational point. Then Kleiman §2 Thm. 2.5 says the
33	   comparison `Pic_{C/k} → Pic_{(C/k)ét}` is already bijective, so the plain
34	   presheaf is the sheaf. This is *strictly weaker* than the challenge, whose
35	   curve need not have a rational point, and it is the route the conditional
36	   `Scheme.picSchemeOfHasRationalPoint` records;
37	2. sheafify. Nothing is assumed about `C(k)`, and the sheaf axiom holds by
38	   construction. This is the route realised here and the one the project
39	   claims (owner decision of 2026-07-28).
40	
41	## The site
42	
43	Mathlib `v4.31` carries the big étale site on schemes,
44	`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.etaleTopology = grothendieckTopology @Etale`
45	(`Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Sites/Etale.lean`). The relative Picard presheaf
46	lives on the slice `Over (Spec k)` rather than on `Scheme`, so the topology is
47	transported along the localisation of SGA 4 III 5.2.1, available in Mathlib as
48	`GrothendieckTopology.over`: a sieve of `T : Over (Spec k)` covers iff the
49	corresponding sieve of `T.left` covers étale-locally. That transport is where
50	"the étale topology on `(Sch/k)`" becomes a definition rather than a parameter,
51	and it is what lets the sheaf property below be a *theorem* rather than a
52	hypothesis.
53	
54	## Main definitions
55	
56	* `Scheme.etaleTopologyOver k` — the étale topology on `(Sch/k) = Over (Spec k)`.
57	* `Scheme.PicSharp.etaleSheaf C` — `Pic_{(C/k)ét}`, a bundled
58	  `Sheaf (etaleTopologyOver k) AddCommGrpCat`, obtained by sheafifying the
59	  relative Picard presheaf.
60	* `Scheme.PicSharp.etaleSheaf_isSheaf` — the sheaf property, extracted as a
61	  standalone statement about the underlying presheaf.
62	* `Scheme.PicScheme.picEt C` — the set-valued functor
63	  `T ↦ Pic_{(C/k)ét}(T)` that the representability obligation is stated
64	  against, together with `picEtComparison C`, the canonical comparison
65	  `picSharp C ⟶ picEt C` from the unsheafified functor.
66	* `Scheme.PicScheme.picEt_isSheaf_forget` — the sheaf property of `picEt`
67	  itself (the group structure forgotten), which is what a representing scheme
68	  must match.
69	
70	## References
71

73	étale-sheaf clause) and Thm. 2.5 (`th:comp`), §4 Thm. `th:main`.

## (1) Carrier match: the two functors are different objects, on four independent axes

`pic0TypeFunctor C` is an `abbrev`, so it unfolds fully (`/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean:58-59`):

```lean
noncomputable abbrev pic0TypeFunctor : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u :=
  (pic0Functor C ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) ⋙ forget GrpCat
```

with object value definitionally `pic0Subgroup C T.unop` (line 62-64, `rfl`). Chasing the chain:

- `pic0Subgroup C T : Subgroup (picEt C T)` = classes of degree zero at *every* field point of `T` (`Pic0Functor.lean:107-118`, `degAt lam t = 0` for all `K`, `t : overSpec k K ⟶ T`).
- `picEt C T : Type u` is **not** a sheafification. It is a bespoke affine-opens limit: `picEtSubgroup C T`, compatible families of `PicEtAff C Γ(T.left,U)` over `T.left.affineOpens` (`PicEt.lean:91-106`).
- `PicEtAff C A : Type u` is a hand-rolled **one-step étale plus construction**: `Quotient (picEtAffSetoid C (A := A))`, i.e. `Σ E : Algebra.EtaleCover A, descentClasses C E` modulo common refinement (`PicEtAff.lean:198-219`).

Against AJC's `PicScheme.picEt` (`/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/PicEtSheaf.lean:221-224`):

```lean
noncomputable def picEt ... : (Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type (u+1) :=
  (PicSharp.etaleSheaf C).obj ⋙ CategoryTheory.forget AddCommGrpCat.{u+1}
```

where `etaleSheaf C = (presheafToSheaf (etaleTopologyOver k) AddCommGrpCat.{u+1}).obj (PicSharp.relPresheaf C)` (`PicEtSheaf.lean:149-153`), and `etaleTopologyOver k = Scheme.etaleTopology.over (Spec (.of k))` (line 105-107).

Concrete mismatches, all four of your candidates fire:

| axis | AJCR `pic0TypeFunctor` | AJC `PicScheme.picEt` |
|---|---|---|
| universe | `Type u` | `Type (u+1)` — carrier is `Quotient (relPicSetoid ...)` over `LineBundle.OnProduct : Type (u+1)` (`LineBundlePullback.lean:136`) |
| domain | `(Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ` — **same slice** | same |
| sheafification | bespoke one-step plus + affine-opens limit, `AJCR PicEtAff.lean:218` | mathlib `presheafToSheaf` at `etaleTopologyOver k` |
| topology of the sheafification | étale *inputs* (`Algebra.EtaleCover`) but the only `IsSheaf` theorem in all of AJCR is Zariski (`Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean:91`, `Presieve.IsSheaf Scheme.zariskiTopology`) | étale, `picEt_isSheaf_forget` (`PicEtSheaf.lean:249-256`) |
| degree part | degree-**zero** subfunctor only (`pic0Subgroup`, `Pic0Functor.lean:107`) | the **whole** Picard functor, all degrees |

So `(pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy X` is **not** the same proposition as `(PicScheme.picEt C).RepresentableBy X` under any plausible identification. `RepresentableBy` is `homEquiv {X} : (X ⟶ Y) ≃ F.obj (op X)` (mathlib `Yoneda.lean:284-288`), so it is only as good as `F.obj` on the nose. Identifying the two would require, minimally: (a) a `Type u ≃ Type (u+1)` ULift transport, (b) a proof that AJCR's plus-construction-of-affine-limits agrees with mathlib's étale sheafification of `relPresheaf` — which is precisely Kleiman 2.5(1) separatedness, and AJCR's file for that half (`EtaleSeparatedness.lean:16`) says in its own header it is "the future home of" `PicEtAff.unit_injective`, with only `unit_injective_of_ker` landed (`EtaleSeparatednessClose.lean:193`), and (c) a degree decomposition splitting off `Pic⁰` from `Pic`, which AJC does not have on `picEt` at all. Note also AJCR has no `PicScheme` namespace and no `Scheme.etaleTopology` reference anywhere outside `Cohomology/`; AJC has no `PicEtAff`, no `pic0Functor`, no `pic0Subgroup`, no `sigmaExtension`, no `degAt`. The two towers share nothing below the interface.

Its named form `IsChartUniv` is a `Prop`-valued *definition*, not a theorem (`Pic0ChartPair.lean:173-178`), and its own docstring says "Stated as a `Prop`-valued definition rather than proved". - `mixedParamRepresentableBy` (`Pic0ChartAtlasParamFree.lean:125-138`) re-binds all three; its own docstring lines 122-124 names what stays hypothetical: "`hf` (i.e. `IsChartUniv`, still CERT-Σ-gated), local surjectivity (DAT-B B-6), and the *existence* of `rep i`".

## (3) The engine is sorry-free and is not vacuous

`Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean` has zero `sorry` in any position. Kernel-verified via LSP: both `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` and `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0SigmaFunctor_isSheaf` report axioms `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]` only. The 135-file import closure of `Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean` contains sorries **only** in `AlgebraicJacobian/Challenge.lean` (the frozen headline gate, reached via `Curve/CrossBaseSquare.lean` etc.), none in the Picard engine chain itself.

Not vacuous, and not the `HasDivFunctor` failure mode. `pic0SigmaSheaf C = ⟨pic0SigmaFunctor C, ...⟩` (`Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean:147-149`), `pic0SigmaFunctor C = Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) (pic0TypeFunctor C)` (line 76-77), whose object value is `Σ a : T.unop ⟶ Spec k, (pic0TypeFunctor C).obj (op (Over.mk a))` = `Σ a, pic0Subgroup C (Over.mk a)` (`OverSigmaExtension.lean:125-126` + `Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean:62`). `C` occurs load-bearingly: `pic0Subgroup C` is a subgroup of `picEt C T`, itself built from `descentClasses C E ≤ relPic C (overSpec k E.Carrier)` (`PicEtAff.lean:76-80`), and `relPic C T = (C ⊗ T).left.CechPic ⧸ picFromBase C T` (`RelPic.lean:63-64`). The curve is inside the carrier, not just in a nonemptiness assertion. The sheaf proof itself (lines 91-142) genuinely consumes curve-specific input: `pic0Subgroup_existsUnique_of_cover` (`PicEtCoverBridge.lean:352`), which needs `[IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] [GeometricallyReduced C.hom] [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom]`.

Importing or transcribing the engine into AJC would discharge **no part** of `fgaPicardRepresentability`, and would not even relocate the sorry — it would add a second, disjoint frontier. Two independent blocks. First, carrier: the engine's conclusion is `(pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy _` at `Type u` over the degree-zero subfunctor of a hand-rolled étale plus (`Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean:166` against `Pic0Functor.lean:151` and `PicEtAff.lean:218`), while the obligation's first conjunct is `Nonempty ((PicScheme.picEt C).RepresentableBy X)` at `Type (u+1)` over mathlib's étale sheafification of the *full* relative Picard presheaf (`FGAPicRepresentability.lean:344` against `PicEtSheaf.lean:221-224`); bridging them requires the universe transport, Kleiman 2.5(1) separatedness (AJCR's own `EtaleSeparatedness.lean:16` is still "the future home of" it), and a degree decomposition AJC does not have. Second, and decisive even if the carriers matched: the engine's three antecedents are **all** unwitnessed binders, so the composite is `hypothesis → hypothesis` with no term at either end — the single sharpest line is `/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/Pic0ChartAtlasParamFree.lean:122-124`, where the strongest packaging in AJCR itself enumerates exactly what remains open (`hf`, coverage, and existence of `rep`), i.e. all three. Nor does the engine touch AJC's other two required conjuncts: it produces `LocallyOfFiniteType` only from per-chart hypotheses (`JacobianDataCharts.lean:154`) and produces `QuasiCompact` rather than `IsSeparated` — grep for `IsSeparated` on the glued object returns nothing. The engine is real, clean, and correctly scoped work on the AJCR carrier; it is not portable value for line 347.
